---
title: "Lab 08 — Controlling for confounders"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
social <- read_csv("data/social.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(messages = factor(
    messages,
    levels = c("Control", "Civic Duty", "Hawthorne", "Neighbors")
  ))
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab08", title = "Controlling for confounders", open = "q4")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "With Control as the reference, the Neighbors coefficient is…",
  q2 = "After adding year of birth, household size, and 2004 turnout, the Neighbors coefficient…",
  q3 = "A confounder is…",
  q4 = "Why is “we controlled for everything” not a causal proof?"
)
```

## What you will do

Compare one treatment coefficient before and after covariates. Adjustment is not a design. Download the `.txt`.

```{r coefs, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=8}
m1 <- lm(primary2006 ~ messages, data = social)
m2 <- lm(primary2006 ~ messages + yearofbirth + hhsize + primary2004, data = social)
coef(m1)["messagesNeighbors"]
coef(m2)["messagesNeighbors"]
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("About 0.08. Assigned the Neighbors mailing, turnout is about 8 points higher than Control.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("About 0.38. That is the turnout rate under the Neighbors mailing."),
  answer("Zero, because the model includes an intercept."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Stays about 0.08. Random assignment already balanced these covariates.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Flips sign, which shows the experiment was confounded."),
  answer("Becomes 1, a perfect effect."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("A variable that influences both the assignment and the outcome.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Any variable you can add to a regression."),
  answer("The outcome measured before treatment, always."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Unmeasured confounders, and controls that sit after the treatment.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
